clinicalProposition.text: Active acromegaly with chronic GH/IGF-I excess is associated with hypertension through several disease-specific mechanisms, including direct renal sodium and water retention with extracellular-volume expansion and vascular effects. The 2026 acromegaly complications consensus reports that GH acts on distal-nephron epithelial sodium channels, that GH promotes nephron sodium retention and expanded extracellular water, and that biochemical control can lower blood pressure in hypertensive patients. This supports a direct-secondary research pathway when acromegaly activity and blood-pressure chronology are documented; it does not establish that every case of hypertension in a person with acromegaly is attributable to acromegaly.

clinicalProposition.text: Hypertension is a common cardiovascular manifestation of clinically established Cushing's syndrome/hypercortisolism. A European Society of Hypertension endocrine-hypertension consensus describes glucocorticoid excess as the biological basis for the cardiovascular damage of endogenous or exogenous Cushing's syndrome and notes that hypertension may persist even after hormone excess is normalized or steroid therapy is discontinued. This supports a direct-secondary research pathway when the Cushing/hypercortisolism diagnosis and blood-pressure chronology are documented, but other primary and secondary causes of hypertension must still be reviewed.

clinicalProposition.text: Chronic kidney disease is a recognized microvascular complication of longstanding type 1 diabetes, but kidney disease in a person with diabetes is not automatically diabetic kidney disease. The 2026 ADA Standards of Care recommend annual urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio and eGFR assessment after at least 5 years of type 1 diabetes and describe the typical diabetic CKD pattern as longstanding diabetes with albuminuria and/or gradual eGFR loss. This supports a disease-progression research pathway when the diabetes duration, renal phenotype, and chronology fit, while active urine sediment, rapid renal decline, nephrotic syndrome, or other atypical features require investigation for alternative kidney disease.

clinicalProposition.text: Sustained high blood pressure is an established risk factor for kidney disease and can participate in a hypertensive target-organ-damage pathway, but chronic kidney disease is etiologically heterogeneous and can also worsen blood pressure. The 2025 AHA/ACC high-blood-pressure guideline identifies chronic kidney disease among conditions whose development is associated with high blood pressure and addresses hypertension treatment in CKD. Individual review therefore requires renal chronology, albuminuria/eGFR patterns, duration and severity of hypertension, and competing renal causes rather than assuming every CKD diagnosis is caused by hypertension.

clinicalProposition.text: Confirmed male hypogonadism/testosterone deficiency is clinically associated with bone loss and can warrant formal osteoporosis and fracture-risk evaluation. The European Academy of Andrology bone-health guideline states that testosterone deficiency may be clearly associated with bone loss and frailty, recommends complete bone-health assessment and DXA in men with confirmed clinical hypogonadism, and notes that evidence that testosterone replacement prevents fractures is lacking. clinicalProposition.text: Prospective cohort evidence supports a temporal association between migraine and later depression. In a large cohort of women without depression at baseline, active migraine with aura, active migraine without aura, and past migraine were each associated with increased incident depression during long-term follow-up, with higher attack frequency associated with greater risk. The evidence does not establish individual causation, is not proof that depression is secondary to migraine in every patient, and should be interpreted with the individual's psychiatric history, headache burden, treatment, sleep, pain, and other competing contributors.

clinicalProposition.text: Pulmonary hypertension is heterogeneous, so this relationship is limited to a documented pulmonary-vascular or pre-capillary phenotype—especially pulmonary arterial hypertension—in which elevated pulmonary vascular load precedes right-ventricular dysfunction and clinically diagnosed right-sided heart failure. The ESC/ERS pulmonary-hypertension guideline describes symptoms as linked to right-ventricular dysfunction and provides a dedicated advanced right-ventricular-failure pathway for patients with pulmonary hypertension. This mapping does not apply when pulmonary hypertension is secondary to pre-existing left-heart failure (group 2 PH), where the direction of the relationship may be reversed, and it does not establish that every diagnosis coded as congestive heart failure was caused by pulmonary hypertension.

clinicalProposition.text: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY: a 63-eye consecutive series with corneal scarring due to bacterial, fungal, and Acanthamoeba keratitis measured opacity grading and higher-order aberrations significantly above normal controls with visual acuity correlating with the aberrations, and a 55-eye keratoplasty series documents herpes simplex keratitis scarring as the surgical indication with a descemetocele or perforation in 13 eyes. publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism METABOLIC_OR_NUTRITIONAL (vitamin D deficiency with dietary calcium deprivation lowering ionised serum calcium, the hypocalcaemic tier of the calcium-deprivation spectrum comprising seizures, tetany, and dilated cardiomyopathy, so neuronal membrane excitability rises), with the rarity, cofactor, and anchor-class limits carried openly: the case report documents an eight-month-old exclusively breastfed boy with three episodes of generalised tonic seizures, total calcium 6.8 mg/dL, ionised calcium 0.91 mmol/L, 25-hydroxyvitamin D 3.5 ng/mL, low phosphate, elevated alkaline phosphatase, and high parathyroid hormone, with mild respiratory alkalosis identified as a further contributor to the ionised-calcium decline and no further seizures after hypocalcaemia correction (PMID 41552144), the emergency-department series of three children documents presentations including a fracture concerning for child abuse, tetany, and hypocalcaemic seizures, all with laboratory and radiographic confirmation of nutritional rickets and resolution with treatment (PMID 14758313), and the population-based study of 23 children with radiographic rickets (17 nutritional) documents presentation features including poor growth in 12, leg deformity in 8, motor delay in 5, leg pain in 3, weakness in 3, and hypocalcaemia or tetany in 2, with incidence rising to 24.1 per 100,000 in children under three in the most recent decade (P=0.003 for trend) (PMID 23374621); the reversible-metabolic rather than structural character is stated - seizure cessation after calcium correction is the hallmark of a metabolic mechanism rather than epilepsy - and the cofactors named are intercurrent febrile illness and respiratory alkalosis; the located evidence is one case report, one three-case series, and a 2-of-17 presentation frequency, so no incidence of seizure as a complication can be estimated, and the population anchor's diagnostic code set included tetany and hypocalcaemic seizure by design; evidenceGaps: All three anchors are small (two case reports and a six-patient series) and the one-seventh frequency statement originates in a single case report's literature summary rather than in a cohort denominator; the two case anchors describe intrinsic parathyroid involvement by the fibrotic process while the surgical anchor describes postoperative deficiency, so no anchor combines both routes in one population; the strongest anchor's hypoparathyroidism was clinically silent and detected on bioassay, so its presence depends on routine parathyroid testing that is not universally performed; the surgical anchor reports only temporary hypoparathyroidism in a series where five of six patients underwent surgery, so it cannot establish how often the deficit follows conservative management.

publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL (visible and burning facial inflammation combined with the survey-anchored rejection-scale experience of being visibly stared at producing anticipatory social threat and avoidance presenting as generalised anxiety, the route the survey anchor models as indirect mediation through quality of life and stigmatisation rather than direct), following the mood-edge convention, with the instrument, missing-comparator, and same-publication null limits carried openly: the Northern Finland Birth Cohort 1966 clinical whole-body examination of 1,932 subjects at 46-year follow-up documents rosacea in 15.1 percent (292 subjects) by dermatologist-performed examination and, after confounder adjustment, an OR of 1.55 (95 percent CI 1.02-2.32) for Hopkins Symptom Checklist-25 psychiatric symptoms with the depression subscale at OR 1.56 (95 percent CI 1.10-2.18) (PMID 38008081), the survey of 168 people with rosacea documents a HADS anxiety score of 7.2 (SD 4.60), HADS depression 5.1 (SD 4.09), Dermatology Life Quality Index 4.05 (SD 4.67), and a rejection scale score of 2.61 (SD 3.37), with path analysis indicating that anxiety and depressive symptoms link to somatic symptoms indirectly, mediated through quality of life and stigmatisation, and that men are more negatively affected (PMID 24088195), and the case-control analysis of 200 Chinese patients against 200 healthy participants documents higher PHQ-9 depression scores and markedly higher Dermatology Life Quality Index scores with 40.5 percent large and 45.5 percent extremely large effect, while finding NO significant association with dry eye syndrome, migraine, hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, Helicobacter pylori, cancer, Crohn's or ulcerative colitis, or chronic kidney disease (PMID 40741710, cross-cited on the dry-eye and migraine edges of this batch for those explicit nulls); the only anchor with a population denominator uses a 25-item screening checklist whose confidence interval is wide at a single-point examination, the survey anchor has no control group so its HADS anxiety mean has no in-study comparator, the third anchor reports depression and quality-of-life instruments rather than any anxiety measure, and no located anchor uses a structured anxiety-disorder diagnostic interview; pre-existing generalised anxiety, social anxiety arising from the facial condition, and the catalog's distinct illness-anxiety-disorder identity are named as alternatives; individual claims route through dated structured anxiety assessment with a dated rosacea diagnosis including severity.

evidenceGaps: The only anchor with a population denominator uses the Hopkins Symptom Checklist-25, a screening instrument whose 95 percent CI of 1.02-2.32 is wide, and applies a single-point 46-year examination rather than incident ascertainment; the survey anchor has no control group, so its HADS anxiety mean of 7.2 has no comparator in the same study; the third anchor reports depression and quality-of-life instruments rather than any anxiety measure and is therefore registered for the quality-of-life and depression context rather than as an anxiety anchor; that same third anchor reports no significant association with several candidate comorbidities, an explicit counterweight carried here; no located anchor uses a structured anxiety-disorder diagnostic interview.

publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism SYSTEMIC_INFLAMMATORY (inflammatory and vascular dysregulation shared between facial skin and ocular surface, with lid-margin inflammation and meibomian gland dysfunction producing a deficient and unstable tear film), following the ocular-manifestation convention (the registered sjogren-s-syndrome and ichthyosis to dry-eye-syndrome edges, and the registered uveitis, hyperopia, and myopia to glaucoma windows owning the anterior-segment and intraocular-pressure routes with sources left untouched per ME-29), with the ascertainment, referral-behaviour, and same-publication null limits carried openly: the multi-institutional case-control study of 12,936 rosacea patients against an equal number of sex- and age-matched controls over 12 years documents adjusted odds ratios of 3.44 (95 percent CI 2.71-4.36) for blepharitis, 1.65 (1.50-1.82) for conjunctivitis, 1.93 (1.70-2.20) for glaucoma, 1.89 (1.70-2.09) for dry eye syndrome, and 3.26 (1.41-7.57) for chalazion (PMID 34209731), the clinical review documents chronic blepharoconjunctivitis with eyelid-margin inflammation and meibomian gland dysfunction as the most common ocular features with corneal complications including vascularisation, ulceration, scarring, and rarely perforation, and notes that diagnosis is often delayed when cutaneous changes are absent, particularly in children (PMID 33403718), and the referral-cohort comparison of 176 patients diagnosed by ophthalmology against 176 diagnosed by dermatology documents meibomian gland dysfunction (P<0.001), telangiectasia (P=0.004), and anterior blepharitis (P=0.008) as significantly higher in the ophthalmology-diagnosed group, concluding lid disease-related manifestations are the major and most observable ocular problems, while corneal, episcleral, scleral, and lens findings did not differ significantly (PMID 12658088); the case-control anchor derives ocular diagnoses from dermatology service records so ocular ascertainment is incomplete for patients not referred, the referral anchor measures which service made the diagnosis rather than prevalence or severity so its positive findings are consistent with referral behaviour alone, a separate 2025 Chinese case-control found no significant association between rosacea and dry eye syndrome (PMID 40741710), and the direction is genuinely bidirectional because ocular rosacea is frequently the presenting sign when cutaneous changes are absent; no glaucoma, conjunctivitis, corneal-scarring, chalazion, or blepharitis edge is registered (window ownership, constitutive proximity, composite endpoint, shared mechanism, and catalog-gap respectively); individual claims route through dated dry-eye diagnosis with objective tear-film or meibomian-gland assessment excluding Sjogren-type dryness, contact-lens use, ocular medications, uveitic dryness, and prior ocular surgery.

evidenceGaps: The case-control anchor derives its ocular diagnoses from dermatology service records, so ocular ascertainment is incomplete for patients not referred to ophthalmology; the referral-comparison anchor measures the difference between which service made the diagnosis, not the prevalence or severity of ocular disease, and its positive findings are consistent with referral behaviour alone; a separate 2025 Chinese case-control analysis of 200 rosacea patients found no significant association with dry eye syndrome, an explicit counterweight carried here; the clinical-review anchor notes that ocular diagnosis is often delayed when cutaneous changes are absent, particularly in children, so ocular-first presentations are systematically under-represented in cutaneous cohorts; the case-control anchor's glaucoma association overlaps a route the registered uveitis and myopia windows already own.

publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism NEUROENDOCRINE_CASCADE (facial neuropeptide release and vasomotor reactivity plausibly lowering the trigeminovascular headache threshold, the route the located literature ties to elevated plasma calcitonin gene-related peptide and to anti-CGRP-associated development of acne and rosacea), following the comorbidity-magnitude convention (the registered ocd, ptsd, abdominal-migraine, alice-in-wonderland-syndrome, cyclic-vomiting-syndrome, and occipital-neuralgia to migraine-headaches edges), with the heterogeneity, bidirectional-prevalence, phenotype-specificity, and same-publication null limits all carried openly: the systematic review and meta-analysis of 11 observational studies including 112,994 rosacea patients and 4,402,330 non-rosacea participants documents migraine prevalence of 25 percent in rosacea patients (95 percent CI 0.15-0.35, I-squared 99 percent) and odds of migraine against controls of 1.93 (95 percent CI 1.42-2.64, I-squared 98 percent, 95 percent prediction interval 0.67-5.53) - a prediction interval that includes the null, so the pooled effect does not hold in every population - while identifying erythematotelangiectatic subtype, female gender, age, and severity as contributing factors (PMID 40899443), the cross-sectional study of 604 patients phenotyped by face-to-face interview with clinical examination documents migraine prevalence of 54 percent in patients with rosacea and rosacea prevalence of 65 percent in patients with migraine, with concomitant migraine associated with flushing (OR 2.6), ocular symptoms (OR 2.4), and burning (OR 2.1) but INVERSELY related to papules and pustules (OR 0.5) (PMID 36341245), and the case-control of 150 rosacea patients against matched controls documents headaches and migraine more prevalent in rosacea patients (P<0.0001 and P=0.0006) with ocular symptoms present in 51.3 percent and more frequent in those with migraine (P=0.03) (PMID 42390920); the cross-sectional anchor conditions on one or the other diagnosis so it establishes overlap rather than temporal sequence, its inverse papule-pustule finding indicates the relationship is phenotype-specific, a separate 2025 Chinese case-control found no significant association with migraine (PMID 40741710), and a shared trigeminal neuropeptide substrate is named as the alternative in which neither condition is causal for the other; sources are disjoint from this batch's rhinitis-vasomotor to migraine-headaches edge (no within-batch sharing); individual claims route through dated ICHD-3 migraine diagnosis with a headache diary and a dated rosacea diagnosis with subtype, excluding medication-over-use headache, migraine predating the skin diagnosis, and concurrent systemic inflammatory disease.

evidenceGaps: The meta-analysis reports I-squared of 99 percent for prevalence and 98 percent for the pooled odds ratio, and its 95 percent prediction interval of 0.67 to 5.53 includes the null, so the pooled effect does not reliably hold in every population studied; the cross-sectional anchor reports prevalence of each condition within the other, so it establishes overlap rather than temporal sequence; that anchor's inverse association for papules and pustules (OR 0.5) indicates the relationship is phenotype-specific and that subtypes differ, which the authors note requires further stratification; the third anchor is a single-centre 150-patient comparison without subtype or ICHD-3 detail in the abstract; a 2025 Chinese case-control analysis of 200 rosacea patients found no significant association with migraine, an explicit counterweight carried here.

publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism PHARMACOLOGICAL_IATROGENIC (lithium concentrates in the thyroid, impairs hormone release and synthesis, and inhibits thyroid hormone signalling at the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis, producing a dose-dependent fall in free thyroxine with compensatory thyroid-stimulating-hormone rise), following the file's own existing rank 1 treatment-mediated convention and the treatment-mediated precedent class (polymyalgia-rheumatica->osteoporosis at glucocorticoid burden, renal-toxicity->chronic-kidney-disease at toxic exposure), with lithium named as the proximate agent and the iatrogenic, detection-bias, and specificity limits carried openly: the Hong Kong incident-bipolar population cohort of 4,752 individuals with mean 8.4-year follow-up reports lithium associated with hypothyroidism (adjusted hazard ratio 2.00, 95 percent CI 1.72-2.33) against non-lithium treatment, a higher-risk gradient at higher serum levels (2.08, 1.67-2.59), reduced thyroid risk with valproate, olanzapine, quetiapine, and risperidone, and derived serum-level thresholds near 0.50 mEq per litre for hypothyroidism (PMID 39932712); the Oxford three-decade laboratory analysis reports adjusted hypothyroidism hazard ratio 2.31 (95 percent CI 2.05-2.60) with women under 60 at greatest risk (PMID 26003379); the US nine-therapy competing-risk analysis of 24,574 patients is registered as an explicit COUNTERWEIGHT rather than as support, reporting a four-year cumulative risk of 8.8 percent on lithium against 6.3 percent on oxcarbazepine with NO statistical difference from quetiapine, overlapping error bars across all nine therapies, and 2.26- to 3.05-fold greater hypothyroidism testing on lithium (PMID 27226264). Null carried openly - the same Hong Kong anchor reports no association with stage 4 or higher chronic kidney disease or end-stage kidney disease despite the stage 3 signal, and the Oxford anchor reports nulls for hyperthyroidism (1.22, 0.96-1.55) and raised adjusted calcium (1.08, 0.88-1.34), establishing the effect's specificity for hypothyroidism. Shared-cause limit: bipolar disorder carries its own independent thyroid autoimmunity signal and no located anchor compares lithium-treated against untreated bipolar patients, so disease and treatment cannot be separated within these designs. Treatment-mediated guard: the exposure throughout is the prescribed medication rather than the psychiatric condition, and the catalog's hypothyroidism identity has seven registered incoming edges, all disease-mediated, with none medication-mediated. DISCLOSED DUPLICATE-SCOPE: the lithium-to-chronic-kidney-disease route is NOT registered here because it is already owned by rel-renal-toxicity-to-chronic-kidney-disease (registered with the Swedish lithium new-user active-comparator cohort, PMID 37418264); the located lithium-to-kidney anchors for this file are the same drug-to-organ pair from a psychiatric indication and are left untouched per ME-29 while the CRG redundancy-semantics question stands at eleven accumulated examples. The parallel research-set pair ptsd->hypothyroidism is withheld as SHARED-ROUTE with this edge, both resting on the same lithium-to-thyroid drug-outcome pair and differing only in prescribing indication. Individual claims require a dated lithium start, stop, dose, and serum-level timeline, dated thyroid studies before and after initiation, a documented lithium-free or alternative-mood-stabiliser interval where one exists, and exclusion of autoimmune thyroiditis, iodine and drug exposure, prior thyroid radioiodine or surgery, pituitary disease, and non-prescribed lithium sources.

evidenceGaps: All three anchors are observational and cannot exclude bipolar disorder's own thyroid autoimmunity as a contributor, because no anchor compares lithium-treated against untreated bipolar patients; the largest anchor reports a null for stage 4 or higher chronic kidney disease and end-stage kidney disease despite a stage 3 signal, so the renal consequence is bounded and the hypothyroidism consequence is not; the US competing-risk anchor reports overlapping confidence intervals across all nine therapies, no statistical difference between lithium and quetiapine, and 2.26- to 3.05-fold greater hypothyroidism testing on lithium, so its hypothyroidism incidence estimate is detection-inflated even though the comparative ranking is informative; no located anchor reports a lithium-free control arm drawn from the same bipolar population; the older prevalence estimate of 10.4 percent overall with 14 percent in women against 4.5 percent in men (PMID 10789300) and the graded thyroid-stimulating-hormone rise by lithium band (PMID 37704933) were located and reviewed but are not among this edge's three registered references because the larger contemporary designs supersede them.

publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is a shared gut-brain behavioural circuit rather than a lesion: repeated postprandial regurgitation, abdominal discomfort, early satiety, and fear of feeding produce food avoidance, meal skipping, and weight loss in rumination syndrome, and a pre-existing eating-disorder framework supplies body-image disturbance and a restrictive behavioural repertoire, with either state able to maintain the other through the well-described feedback loop in which restriction worsens postprandial discomfort and in which regurgitation relieves the discomfort of eating; the loop is named as the plausible common pathway because the located cohorts report the comorbidity without experimentally separating the direction, and whether one condition recruits or maintains the other in any given patient remains hypothesized until the chronology of onset is documented. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at matched case-control, adolescent case-series, and bidirectional paediatric-cohort class following the file's own gastrointestinal and behavioural framing and the registry's treatment- and behaviour-mediated precedent classes: the case-control anchor is the only located design with a matched comparison group and is the anchor that supplies the effect sizes, the significance thresholds, and the independent-adjusted odds ratio, and it is registered together with its own directional framing (PMID 33988353); the adolescent case series supplies the contemporary paediatric observation and the explicit caution that diagnosis is frequently delayed because the presentation is mistaken for reflux or vomiting (PMID 42217214); the bidirectional cohort is registered as the anchor that bounds the claim by showing the comorbidity is concentrated in the adolescent-onset stratum and absent in the early-onset stratum, which is direct evidence against a single uniform mechanism across all rumination syndrome (PMID 38504395). Because the largest anchor models the relationship in the opposite direction to the edge's name, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, records the direction as unresolved in the causation status, and routes individual attribution through dated, separately signed diagnoses of each condition plus clinician exclusion of learned vomiting or learned regurgitation. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established in either direction, and the located anchor argues actively against fixing a direction: the largest comparative study modelled prior eating-disorder history as a risk factor for rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 rather than modelling rumination syndrome as a risk factor for a later eating-disorder diagnosis, so the temporal ordering is asserted by that design rather than demonstrated by it; a substantial share of the apparent overlap is plausibly diagnostic rather than causal, because rumination syndrome is classified within the feeding and eating disorders in current diagnostic nomenclature and a prior eating-disorder label may reflect reclassification of the same undifferentiated regurgitation behaviour rather than a distinct illness preceding it; the two entities also differ in mechanism, since rumination syndrome is an effortless postprandial retrograde flow of undigested contents driven by an automatic autonomic reflex, whereas bulimia nervosa is a deliberate binge-and-purge behaviour, so shared abdominal distress, dietary restriction, and body-image disturbance can produce convergent presentations without either driving the other; and the adolescent anchors are a case series and a single-centre bidirectional cohort, neither of which includes a rumination-syndrome-free comparison group for the eating-disorder outcome. Individual claims require a dated, separately signed diagnosis of bulimia nervosa with documented binge and purge episodes, a dated rumination-syndrome diagnosis documenting effortless regurgitation of undigested food, the chronology of which diagnosis came first, and explicit clinician exclusion of vomiting as a learned behaviour or of regurgitation as a learned behaviour before the two are recorded as co-occurring. Evidence gaps carried openly: All three anchors are observational and none establishes temporal order; the largest anchor is a single-tertiary-centre case-control study of 24 cases, so its adjusted odds ratio of 16.4 rests on few exposed individuals and is vulnerable to wide confidence intervals that the abstract does not report; the direction of the model is reversed relative to the edge, so it cannot be cited as evidence that rumination syndrome produces a later eating-disorder diagnosis; the adolescent case series has no comparison group and reports six of eight referred patients, a referral-enriched sample; the bidirectional cohort reports mood comorbidity percentages but not eating-disorder prevalence stratified by onset group, so the claim that the eating-disorder overlap is concentrated in adolescent-onset disease is carried from the depression and anxiety figures rather than from a reported eating-disorder comparison; no located anchor measures regurgitant characteristics such as acidity or enamel exposure, so the rumination-syndrome-to-dental-erosion route was reviewed and withheld as MECHANISM-UNSUPPORTED, because undigested regurgitation is qualitatively different from the acid-laden self-induced vomiting of bulimia nervosa, and the published dental-erosion evidence in this space is drawn from eating-disorder populations rather than from rumination syndrome cohorts. Alternatives requiring exclusion before any individual attribution: Bulimia nervosa or binge-eating disorder as a pre-existing, independently diagnosed condition whose behavioural effects may drive food avoidance and regurgitation; Diagnosed vomiting as a learned or intentional behaviour, which would reclassify the presentation away from rumination syndrome entirely; Gastroesophageal reflux disease, achalasia, and delayed gastric emptying, which were excluded in the located cohorts by normal gastric emptying studies but must be excluded individually; Organic CNS disease, in which one adolescent case in the located series was found to have an underlying organic medical illness. Anchors: PMID 33988353, PMID 42217214, PMID 38504395. The conservative framing records the direction of the relationship as unresolved and notes openly that the largest anchor models the association in the reverse direction, names the shared gut-brain feedback loop as a hypothesized rather than demonstrated mechanism, bounds the claim with the onset-stratum finding showing the comorbidity is not uniform across rumination syndrome, and requires dated separate diagnoses plus exclusion of learned behaviour before any individual attribution.

publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is a shared emotion-regulation circuit operating through the gut-brain axis together with a reactive distress pathway: repetitive negative thinking about eating and the body, avoidance of public eating, and rumination in the cognitive sense are all documented transdiagnostic features that maintain each other, while the physical experience of effortless regurgitation, meal avoidance, and visible weight loss supplies an independent and sufficient reason for anxiety to develop; the pathway is named as a two-part mechanism because the located evidence supports the reactive route as the more readily documented and the shared-circuit route as the more speculative, and which route predominates in any given patient remains hypothesized until the anxiety chronology is established relative to regurgitation onset. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at matched case-control, adolescent case-series, and bidirectional paediatric-cohort class alongside the file's rank 1 eating-disorder edge, which shares the same three anchors because the largest comparative study reports both as components of a single 83.3 percent psychiatric-disorder figure rather than as separable findings: the case-control anchor supplies the only comparison group and the only adjusted estimate (PMID 33988353); the case series supplies the adolescent observation and the documented diagnostic-delay mechanism (PMID 42217214); and the bidirectional cohort supplies the onset-stratum bound showing anxiety is concentrated in adolescent-onset disease and is comparatively uncommon in early-childhood-onset disease (PMID 38504395). Because the largest anchor's direction is reversed relative to the edge and because the reactive pathway is at least as plausible as the shared-circuit pathway, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only, records direction as unresolved, and routes individual attribution through dated diagnoses on both sides with explicit separation of situational from pre-existing anxiety. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation of anxiety is established for any individual, and the direction is unresolved for the same reasons that apply to the file's eating-disorder edge: the largest comparative anchor modelled psychiatric-disorder history as a risk factor FOR rumination syndrome at an adjusted odds ratio of 4.47, not rumination syndrome as a risk factor for a subsequent anxiety diagnosis, so the temporal ordering is a design choice rather than a finding; a substantial component of the overlap is plausibly reactive rather than causal, because a chronic, visible, embarrassing, and socially stigmatising regurgitation behaviour with associated weight loss and meal avoidance is an obvious precipitant of anxiety and of social avoidance, and the located series documents embarrassment and distress as central features without establishing whether any anxiety preceded them; the two conditions also share a documented transdiagnostic mechanism in which repetitive negative thinking and emotion-regulation difficulty appear in both, which permits either condition to recruit the other; and no located anchor measures anxiety before the onset of regurgitation. Individual claims require a dated anxiety diagnosis with documented symptom history predating or postdating regurgitation onset, a dated rumination-syndrome diagnosis, and clinician separation of situational anxiety about the illness from a pre-existing anxiety disorder. Evidence gaps carried openly: All three anchors are observational and none establishes temporal order; the case-control anchor reports 83.3 percent psychiatric-disorder prevalence against 50.0 percent in controls, but the 50 percent control figure is itself high and indicates that the comparison group was not a healthy population, which narrows the interpretable effect; the psychiatric-disorder exposure in that study is a composite and the anxiety-specific contribution is reported as 37.5 percent of cases without a matching control percentage, so the anxiety-specific risk difference cannot be reconstructed from the abstract; the adolescent case series is a referral-enriched series of eight referred patients with no comparison group; the bidirectional cohort reports anxiety by onset stratum but not by severity, treatment, or duration, and its adolescent-onset group is overwhelmingly female, so sex composition is an uncontrolled confounder; no located anchor uses a structured anxiety instrument reported in the abstract, and no anchor separates pre-existing from reactive anxiety, which is the single most important unresolved question for this edge. The file's depressive-disorder route was reviewed and withheld as DUPLICATE-SCOPE rather than authored, because the registry already carries bulimia-nervosa to depressive-disorder and anxiety-disorder to depressive-disorder, so a third direct rumination-syndrome to depressive-disorder edge would duplicate a relationship the graph already resolves through two registered chains. Alternatives requiring exclusion before any individual attribution: Pre-existing anxiety disorder predating the onset of regurgitation, which would reverse the presumed reactive direction; Situtional or illness-related anxiety about regurgitation in public, which is a consequence rather than a co-occurring disorder; Gastroesophageal reflux disease, functional dyspepsia, and other organic gastrointestinal causes of regurgitation; Developmental delay and neurodevelopmental comorbidity, reported at 24 percent in the early-childhood-onset stratum of the located cohort. Anchors: PMID 33988353, PMID 42217214, PMID 38504395. publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism POST_SURGICAL_OR_TREATMENT, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is destruction of functional salivary acinar tissue, either by direct tumour infiltration replacing gland parenchyma or by surgical resection removing it, and independently by the dose of ionizing radiation delivered to the contralateral and residual salivary tissue during adjuvant treatment, with radiation damage producing loss of secretory function and chronic reduction in salivary flow as the proximate mechanism and the resulting patient-reported dry mouth as the clinical expression; the treatment vector is the one the located evidence documents mechanistically, the disease-and-resection vector is the one carried as hypothesized because no located anchor measures it, and which predominates in an individual depends on subsite, laterality, and whether the contralateral gland lay within the irradiated field. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at mechanistic-review, rapid-evidence-review, and survivorship-retrospective class, and it is the file's first edge to the xerostomia identity, which had zero registered incoming edges and zero outgoing edges before this batch: the mechanistic review is the anchor that supplies the actual causal chain from radiation exposure to acinar secretory loss to patient-reported xerostomia and is the only located source that describes the intermediate mechanism (PMID 38808518); the rapid evidence review supplies the general salivary-gland-disorder framing and is reused rather than duplicated, since its source entity pmid-38905553 was already registered in the master source registry and this edge therefore adds a reference use without adding a new source entity (PMID 38905553); and the survivorship cohort establishes population relevance in treated malignant parotid disease while being registered with the explicit caveat that its located abstract reports no xerostomia instrument or prevalence (PMID 38837232). publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism SYSTEMIC_INFLAMMATORY, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is a shared type-2 inflammatory circuit with abnormal arachidonic acid metabolism producing the characteristic upper and lower airway phenotype, in which the same inflammatory process is expressed as nasal polyposis and chronic rhinosinusitis in the upper airway and as asthma in the lower airway, and in which cyclooxygenase-1 inhibition by aspirin or other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs shunts arachidonic acid toward cysteinyl leukotrienes, amplifying the same inflammation; the circuit is named as unified precisely because the located evidence describes the upper and lower airway manifestations as one process rather than as sequential spread, and the resulting clinical pattern is a single inflammatory disease presenting in two anatomical compartments rather than one condition causing another. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at mechanistic-review, unified-airway-review, and clinical-practice-guideline class, and at a deliberately different strength from a causal edge: both edges in this file are definitional co-occurrences rather than causal progressions, and the conservative standard therefore frames them as co-occurrences requiring INDEPENDENT clinical documentation rather than as consequences of the syndrome, with each target's own separate documentation, treatment, and objective testing required before the condition can be treated as established. The mechanistic review supplies the composite phenotype definition and the severe, recurrent, aggressive-polyposis characterisation (PMID 39665076); the unified-airway review supplies the arachidonic-acid mechanism, the drug-trigger relation, and the explicit statement that conventional management of both the asthma and the chronic rhinosinusitis components is often inadequate (PMID 36283868); and the adult sinusitis clinical practice guideline supplies the current diagnostic and management standard against which the sinus component must be evaluated (PMID 40741969). Because the relationship is definitional rather than causal, the conservative standard holds both edges at ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED and requires separate signed documentation for each component rather than permitting the composite label to substitute for it. Causation and direction limits: No causal claim is made or available here, and the edge's own causation status says so directly: chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyposis is one of the three criteria that define this syndrome, so an assertion that the syndrome produces the sinusitis is circular and is expressly disclaimed rather than argued. What the edge records is a co-occurrence with a distinct operational consequence, namely that a veteran whose record carries only the label Samter's triad has not thereby had chronic rhinosinusitis independently documented, characterised by extent, side, and severity, or linked to a treatment plan, and the located evidence shows this matters because the sinus disease is described as highly aggressive, recurrent, and frequently requiring repeat endoscopic sinus surgery. The treatment gradient is also carried openly: the located reviews attribute symptom improvement to surgery plus desensitization, which means the functional burden attributed to the syndrome is partly treatment-dependent and cannot be assigned to disease alone. Individual claims require a dated otolaryngology assessment with endoscopy or imaging documenting chronic rhinosinusitis independently of the triad label, documented extent and polyp burden, and a treatment timeline. Evidence gaps carried openly: All three anchors describe the syndrome rather than testing an exposure-outcome relationship, so none of them is evidence of causation and none should be cited as such; the two review articles are narrative syntheses without systematic search, without quality appraisal reported in the abstract, and without pooled estimates; the characterisation of highly aggressive recurrent ethmoidal polyposis and of difficult-to-treat asthma is qualitative and unreferenced in the located abstracts, so its magnitude cannot be quantified from these sources; the clinical practice guideline covers adult sinusitis generally rather than the aspirin-exacerbated subtype, so it supplies the standard of evaluation rather than syndrome-specific evidence; and the located abstracts report no prevalence of chronic rhinosinusitis within diagnosed syndrome cohorts, because by definition all of them have it, which is the clearest demonstration that this edge carries no epidemiological information beyond the definition. publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism MULTIFACTORIAL, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is a paraprotein-mediated contribution to dermal mucin deposition, in which clonal immunoglobulin produced by a plasma-cell clone is proposed to drive the fibroblast response and excessive dermal mucin accumulation that defines scleredema, with the alternative and simpler reading being that both the skin disease and the plasma-cell dyscrasia arise from a shared underlying state and that the paraprotein is a marker rather than an agent; the mechanism is classified MULTIFACTORIAL because the located evidence cannot choose between the paraprotein-as-agent and paraprotein-as-marker readings, and the clinical consequence is the same under either: a patient carrying scleredema warrants plasma-cell screening, and a patient carrying an established plasma-cell dyscrasia warrants a skin examination. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at case-report and multicentre-retrospective class, and at the weakest strength of the three edges in this file, which the conservative standard records explicitly rather than smoothing over: the primary anchor is a single case report of a restrictive pattern attributed to cutaneous hardness, the multicentre series supplies disease-severity and treatment context but reports NO pulmonary outcomes, and the third anchor supplies parenchymal fibrosis in a patient whose lung findings are confounded by myeloma and by the excluded systemic sclerosis differential. The case report is the anchor that supplies the explicit mechanical statement that cutaneous hardness may cause limited mobility with respiratory manifestations mainly in extensive disease (PMID 33865279); the multicentre series is registered for the chronic-debility and treatment-resistance context and is explicit in the evidence gaps that it reports no pulmonary outcome data (PMID 26304054); and the scleroderma-mimic case is registered for the parenchymal-fibrosis observation with its full confounding disclosed, so that a reviewer sees the countervailing evidence rather than a clean association (PMID 30088450). publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is age-related fibroelastic replacement of the sinus node and atrioventricular conduction tissue, which slows impulse formation and conduction and produces the bradycardic pole, with the same degenerative process extending to the atrial myocardium as electrical and structural remodelling that lowers the threshold for reentrant atrial fibrillation and produces the tachycardic pole. The mechanism is named as a shared degenerative substrate rather than a causal sequence because the located evidence reports a bidirectional relationship and a remodelling association, and does not establish that sinus node degeneration produces atrial remodelling rather than both reflecting a common ageing substrate, which is also why the located review describes the overlap in terms of age-related degeneration of the cardiac conduction system. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analytic, randomised-controlled-trial, and literature-review class, following the file's existing cardiovascular pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that supplies the pooled direction of travel and the explicit bidirectionality statement together with the pacing-strategy gradient, which is the located evidence that atrial fibrillation burden in this population is at least partly treatment-dependent (PMID 37023861). The randomised trial is the anchor that supplies the 46 percent atrial fibrillation prevalence in a defined cohort and, more importantly, serves as an EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT, because it is a negative trial showing that reducing atrial pacing did not reduce atrial fibrillation, so the mechanism cannot be stated as simple pacing-induced (PMID 37638973). The literature review supplies the remodelling mechanism and the named co-contributors that must be excluded (PMID 40607080). Because the evidence is bidirectional and partly confounded by the very treatment these patients receive, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, records the negative trial on the face of the edge, and requires a temporal determination before any individual attribution. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence describes a shared substrate rather than a one-directional cause. The meta-analysis describes the sick sinus syndrome and atrial fibrillation relationship as bidirectional and does not establish which precedes which (PMID 37023861). The randomised trial enrolled patients who ALREADY had an indication for first pacemaker implantation, so its 46 percent atrial fibrillation endpoint describes an advanced-disease population, and it is a NEGATIVE trial for the pacing intervention, finding that atrial pacing minimisation did NOT reduce atrial fibrillation incidence, which argues against the simple hypothesis that excess atrial pacing is the driver. The literature review supplies a plausible unifying mechanism, atrial electrical and structural remodelling, but states it as the pathophysiology of the overlap rather than as a demonstrated causal sequence from sinus node disease to atrial fibrillation (PMID 40607080). Individual claims require a dated diagnosis of sick sinus syndrome, objective evidence of the atrial arrhythmia on a dated tracing or monitoring record, and a clinical determination of which condition is temporally antecedent, because the two are frequently recorded together as tachy-bradyarrhythmia rather than as one producing the other, and because pacing strategy, which the located evidence shows materially affects atrial fibrillation risk, is itself a treatment variable rather than a fixed feature of the disease. Evidence gaps carried openly: The primary anchor is a meta-analysis of observational studies and reports heterogeneity across included therapy comparisons without a pooled effect size for the core new-onset atrial fibrillation claim (PMID 37023861). The randomised trial is a NEGATIVE trial, its null result argues against the pacing-exposure mechanism, and its population is restricted to patients with a first pacemaker indication, so it cannot be read as a community prevalence of atrial fibrillation in sick sinus syndrome (PMID 37638973). The third anchor is a literature review rather than primary data (PMID 40607080). NO located anchor establishes temporal order between the two diagnoses in an unselected individual, and the located evidence shows pacing mode itself changes atrial fibrillation risk, so any individual claim must separate disease effect from treatment effect. The syncope route was withheld as EVIDENCE-INSUFFICIENT because the located anchors address syncope as a safety endpoint of pacing programming or as a symptom of a different physiology, and no anchor quantifies syncope as a complication of sinus node disease itself. The implantable-cardiac-pacemaker route was withheld as TREATMENT-CONSEQUENCE rather than a medical secondary condition, the located evidence being entirely about implantation decisions and outcomes. Alternatives requiring exclusion before any individual attribution: Atrial fibrillation as the coexisting or antecedent condition in a tachy-bradyarrhythmia presentation, since the located evidence describes the relationship as bidirectional rather than one-directional; Medication effect, named by the located review as a significant contributor alongside the conduction disease, including rate-limiting and AV-nodal blocking drugs; Atrioventricular nodal block, named as a co-contributor and as a distinct catalog identity, which must be separated from sinus node disease before the bradycardic pole is attributed; Pacing strategy and percentage of atrial pacing, which the located randomised trial shows materially affects atrial fibrillation risk independently of the underlying disease. Anchors: PMID 37023861, PMID 37638973, PMID 40607080. publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism THROMBOTIC_OR_VASCULAR, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is thromboembolic stroke arising from an atrial substrate shared with the sinus node disorder, in which the same age-related fibrotic and remodelling process that slows sinus node impulse formation also alters atrial architecture, creating stasis, appendicular flow reduction and an arrhythmogenic substrate that permits thrombus formation and embolisation to the cerebral circulation. The vector is named as a shared atrial substrate rather than a direct sinus-to-brain pathway because the located evidence reports the association in patients with ISOLATED sinus node dysfunction without atrial fibrillation, which is what the UK Biobank analysis interprets as evidence for a left atrial myopathy, and because a thromboembolic mechanism cannot be assumed in the absence of demonstrated atrial thrombus or appendicular stasis in any given individual. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at meta-analytic, prospective-population-cohort, and hospital-based-cohort class, following the file's existing cardiovascular pathway scope. The meta-analysis is the anchor that supplies the pooled annual stroke incidence of 1.542 percent and, critically, the finding that ISOLATED sinus node dysfunction and sinus node dysfunction with atrial fibrillation carry a similar risk, which is what prevents this edge from collapsing into the already-registered atrial fibrillation route (PMID 37977871). The UK Biobank analysis is the anchor that supplies the large-population effect estimate (subdistribution hazard ratio 2.28) and the explicit left atrial myopathy interpretation that motivates the mechanism category, and its deliberate exclusion of prior stroke and valvular disease is what makes the estimate a clean signal rather than a restatement of baseline risk (PMID 40315941). The Taiwanese cohort is registered as the EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT and as the source of the most clinically actionable nuance: it shows the association is concentrated in patients whose CHA2DS2-VASC score is low, which is precisely the population standard risk stratification would not flag, and it does so in a hospital-based sample with a strict pacemaker-requiring definition of sick sinus syndrome (PMID 41317944). Because the design is confounding-by-indication throughout, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, requires documented AF status and a documented CHA2DS2-VASC score, and states the unresolved anticoagulation question in the causation status rather than implying an established preventive. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence is a risk-marker relationship rather than a demonstrated embolic mechanism. The meta-analysis reports a similar stroke incidence in isolated sinus node dysfunction and in sinus node dysfunction with atrial fibrillation, and its own conclusion is that patients with sinus node dysfunction carry a SIMILAR RISK of stroke to those with combined sinus node dysfunction and atrial fibrillation, with future studies needed to investigate whether stroke-prevention interventions such as anticoagulation can help (PMID 37977871), which is an explicit statement that the mechanism and the intervention are unresolved. The UK Biobank analysis is observational and interprets its finding through a proposed left atrial myopathy rather than a demonstrated one, and it deliberately excludes prosthetic heart valves, rheumatic mitral valve disease, mitral stenosis and prior ischaemic stroke, so its estimate applies to a comparatively lower-risk population (PMID 40315941). The Taiwanese cohort is HOSPITAL-BASED and defines sick sinus syndrome STRICTLY as symptomatic sinus node dysfunction requiring pacemaker implantation, so it is confounded by indication: the patients with sick sinus syndrome were older, more often female, and had higher CHADS2 and CHA2DS2-VASc scores, and after CHA2DS2-VASc adjustment the association was strongest precisely where the score was lowest, which is the signature of a risk marker adding information beyond standard stroke-risk stratification rather than of an independent embolic cause (PMID 41317944). Individual claims require a dated diagnosis of sinus node dysfunction, a dated ischaemic stroke event with imaging or equivalent objective confirmation, a documented atrial fibrillation status, and a documented CHA2DS2-VASc score, because the located evidence shows the strength of this association depends on both the AF status and the baseline stroke score, and because no located anchor establishes that anticoagulation prevents stroke in sinus node dysfunction without atrial fibrillation. Evidence gaps carried openly: The primary anchor pools only 6 studies and its atrial fibrillation subgroup confidence interval is wide and includes values from 0.705 to 2.615 percent, so the isolated-versus-combined similarity finding rests on imprecise data (PMID 37977871). The UK Biobank analysis had only 593 participants with ISOLATED sinus node dysfunction, so the headline subdistribution hazard ratio of 2.28 rests on a small exposed group within a very large cohort and is derived from ICD-coded registry linkage rather than adjudicated clinical diagnosis (PMID 40315941). The third anchor is hospital-based, defines sick sinus syndrome as requiring pacemaker implantation, and the exposed group is confounded by age, sex and baseline stroke score, with the association attenuating to non-significance in patients with CHA2DS2-VASC scores above 2 (PMID 41317944). publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism NEUROLOGICAL_DEGENERATION, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is episodic cerebral hypoperfusion during pauses in sinus node impulse formation or sinoatrial conduction block, so that a period of bradycardia or asystole produces a transient drop in cardiac output and therefore in cerebral perfusion, which the patient experiences as lightheadedness, disorientation or near-syncope, and which, when prolonged or recurrent, produces falls with injury or fracture. The vector is named as a haemodynamic consequence of the same degenerative process that produces the bradycardia rather than as a separate neurological lesion, because the located evidence attributes the symptom to the pacing-sensitive bradycardia rather than to any structural brain change, and the same anchors require that sleep apnoea and medication effect be excluded first, since both can produce identical symptoms without any cerebral hypoperfusion. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at cohort, narrative-review, and case-report class, following the file's existing cardiovascular pathway scope. The cohort study is the anchor that supplies the quantitative symptom burden, dizziness in 45 percent of patients before implantation and 12 percent after, together with the falls and fracture figures and the authors' own statement that no causal relationship could be established (PMID 27702858). The closed-loop stimulation review is the anchor that supplies the plain statement of the symptom triad and the chronotropic-incompetence framing, and its manufacturer-affiliations are disclosed as a source-quality caveat rather than suppressed (PMID 40388576). Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at register-cohort, cross-sectional cohort, and histopathology case-report class, following the file's existing haematological and immune pathway scope. The 244-patient study is the anchor that shows the objective salivary findings are SEVEREST in the lymphoma-affected subgroups, which is the located reason a change in gland status in this population warrants attention (PMID 30120806). The histopathology report is the anchor that documents the morphological spectrum from lymphoepithelial sialadenitis through low-grade MALT lymphoma to high-grade transformation, which is the only located source that states the progression directly (PMID 20551561). The third anchor is a SINGLE-CASE report and supplies no estimate (PMID 20551561). publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is that a tear of the superior glenoid labrum disrupts the biceps anchor and the labral bumper that normally deepens the glenoid socket, so the humeral head loses both its concavity constraint and the counterforce supplied by the long head of the biceps, and the resulting increased translation of the humeral head during elevation and rotation produces the sensation and examination findings of glenohumeral instability and the catching pain of impingement. The mechanism is named as altered joint geometry and lost restraint rather than as a single torn fibre, because the located evidence attributes the clinical significance of the tear to its effect on stability rather than to the tissue itself, and because the same anchors report the symptom pattern as vague and inconsistent rather than as a reproducible mechanical sign. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at retrospective-multicentre-series, systematic-review, and treatment-outcome-systematic-review class, following the file's existing musculoskeletal pathway scope. The multicentre series is the anchor that supplies the Snyder type distribution with 53 percent type II, the injury-mechanism breakdown, and the load-bearing conclusion that only types II, IV and V are unstable (PMID 9848599). The non-operative review is the anchor that supplies the clinical course, return to play in 53.7 percent overall rising to 78 percent on completing rehabilitation, and the explicit list of failure factors including concomitant rotator cuff injury (PMID 35063641). The biceps tenodesis review is the anchor that supplies the high rate of FAILED PRIOR LABRAL REPAIR, 0 to 44 percent, which is the located reason the structural lesion is clinically consequential rather than incidental, together with the complication range (PMID 32579853). Because the target identity is a composite impingement-or-instability label rather than the lesion itself, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, requires the tear type and imaging modality to be documented, and requires the complaint to be attributed to the labral lesion rather than to accompanying pathology. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the target identity is a composite label that the located evidence does not map onto directly. The catalog identity shoulder-condition is Shoulder Impingement / Instability, carrying the aliases instability and shoulder impingement, whereas a labral tear is a STRUCTURAL LESION of the labral complex and the located evidence describes it in terms of the instability it produces rather than reporting an impingement or instability diagnosis as the outcome, so the edge asserts that the tear presents as, and is treated as, an instability problem rather than that it produces either named entity in a diagnostic sense. The primary anchor is explicit that patients' complaints and clinical symptoms are VAGUE AND INCONSISTENT and that imaging was obtained in only a minority of cases, which is a diagnostic-uncertainty statement as much as a clinical one, and it is a 23-lesion series from the pre-MRI era (PMID 9848599). The second anchor is a non-operative treatment-outcome review in athletes, so its outcomes describe athletic function rather than the diagnostic or symptomatic consequences of a tear, and its failure factors are predictors of failed non-operative management rather than consequences of the tear itself (PMID 35063641). The third anchor is a treatment-outcome systematic review in a population selected for failed prior repair (PMID 32579853). Individual claims require a dated labral tear diagnosis with the imaging modality and the tear type documented, since the primary anchor states that only types II, IV and V are unstable and that two of its 23 lesions were in fact anatomic variants, together with a documented functional limitation and a clinical determination that the presenting complaint is attributable to the labral lesion rather than to the impingement or rotator cuff pathology that commonly accompanies it. The second anchor is a non-operative treatment review whose population is athletes, 162 of 244 elite or higher-level, so its failure factors are conditioned on athletic demand and its return-to-play rates are not transferable to a non-athletic population (PMID 35063641). The third anchor is a treatment-outcome review whose population is selected for prior failure, 0 to 44 percent with a failed previous labral repair, and only one of its eight studies included patients with concomitant rotator cuff repair (PMID 32579853). NO located anchor reports the incidence of a superior labral tear in an unselected population, because the lesion is diagnosed only in patients already referred for shoulder symptoms and usually only after imaging, so the relationship recorded here is a relationship among symptomatic referred patients and not a population risk. The rotator-cuff-injury route was authored separately but is a SIBLING rather than a duplicate, since the two coexist in the same shoulder and the located evidence treats them as co-pathology rather than as cause and effect. publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism BIOMECHANICAL_ALTERATION, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is a shared loading history rather than a lesion-to-lesion sequence, in which repetitive overhead throwing or a single traumatic event loads the glenohumeral joint so that the superior labrum and the rotator cuff tendons are stressed in the same movement, so that a patient with one lesion has an elevated likelihood of carrying the other through a common exposure rather than because one injured structure mechanically destroys the other. The vector is deliberately named as shared exposure, which is the only reading the located evidence supports, and it is stated that way precisely because the located cohort shows the co-occurring lesion is often clinically silent, so a shared-exposure explanation does not require the second lesion to be consequential. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at systematic-review, systematic-review, and retrospective-cohort-with-nested-case-control class, following the file's existing musculoskeletal pathway scope. The non-operative review is the anchor that names concomitant rotator cuff injury as a factor associated with failure of non-surgical management (PMID 35063641). The older-patient surgical review is the anchor that states the practical consequence directly, that with concomitant rotator cuff tears the evidence favours debridement or biceps tenotomy over labral repair (PMID 24961444). The military cadet cohort is registered as the EXPLICIT COUNTERWEIGHT and is the reason this edge is ranked second rather than first, because it is a cohort with a matched case-control analysis rather than a review, it reports a 5.56 percent co-occurrence, and it found NO ASSOCIATION WITH INFERIOR OUTCOMES (PMID 35412499). A fourth reviewed anchor reporting a 10 percent rotator cuff incidence among superior labral lesions is recorded in the evidence gaps and deliberately not registered, because registering it would have required exceeding the three-reference cap. Because the located evidence disagrees on whether the co-occurrence matters, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, records the disagreement on the face of the edge, and requires separate documentation of each lesion. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and this edge exists precisely because the located evidence does NOT agree that the co-occurrence is clinically important. A rotator cuff tear coexisting with a labral tear is a CO-PATHOLOGY found in the same shoulder, and the direction between them is not established: the two share a mechanism in that overhead loading or a single traumatic event can injure both, and the located evidence does not demonstrate that one produces the other. The two systematic reviews and the cohort in this edge reach opposite practical conclusions. The non-operative review names concomitant rotator cuff injury as a factor associated with failure of non-surgical management (PMID 35063641) and the older-patient surgical review states that with concomitant tears the evidence favours debridement or biceps tenotomy over labral repair (PMID 24961444), while the military cadet cohort found the co-occurrence in only 5.56 percent and that its presence was NOT ASSOCIATED WITH INFERIOR CLINICAL OUTCOMES (PMID 35412499). A fourth anchor, reviewed and deliberately not registered, reports a still lower 10 percent rotator cuff incidence among superior labral lesions and describes that as a RELATIVELY LOW INCIDENCE, which is a further anchor pointing the same way as the cadet cohort. Individual claims therefore cannot treat the coexistence as established, and an individual attribution requires a dated labral tear diagnosis and a separately dated rotator cuff diagnosis, each with imaging, together with a clinical determination of which lesion is generating the presenting complaint, because the located evidence shows the two are routinely operated on together and that operating on the labrum alone may be the wrong procedure in their presence. Evidence gaps carried openly: Two of the three anchors are systematic reviews of surgical management rather than studies of the natural history of the co-pathology, so both are conditioned on patients who reached the operating theatre, which is the population in which a coexisting rotator cuff lesion is most likely to be found and repaired, and neither reports whether the rotator cuff lesion was symptomatic (PMID 24961444, PMID 35063641). The third anchor is a single-academy cohort of young military cadets with a mean age of 20.53 years undergoing shoulder stabilisation, so its 5.56 percent co-occurrence and its null outcome finding may not generalise to the older patients who make up most superior labral tear surgical series (PMID 35412499). The three anchors also measure different things: treatment failure, treatment choice, and postoperative outcome. NO located anchor establishes that a rotator cuff lesion is caused by a labral tear or vice versa, and none reports the prevalence of either lesion in an unselected population. The shouldeR-condition edge in this file is a sibling rather than a duplicate, since a labral tear and a rotator cuff tear are distinct lesions that the located literature repeatedly treats as coexisting rather than as sequential. Anchors: PMID 35063641, PMID 24961444, PMID 35412499. publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is sleep fragmentation and the psychosocial burden of an involuntary behaviour, in which repeated partial arousals from sleep disrupt sleep architecture and reduce restorative sleep, producing fatigue and daytime sleepiness, while the loss of control and the risk of injuring oneself or a bed partner produce distress, and the combination yields depressive symptoms. The vector is named as a burden and fragmentation pathway rather than as a shared neural circuit, because the located evidence establishes co-occurrence and states its own bidirectionality, and a shared-circuit explanation would require evidence that the same mechanism produces both conditions, which no located anchor provides. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at prospective-case-control, specialist-video-polysomnography-cohort, and PRISMA-P-systematic-review class, following the file's existing psychiatric, neuropsychiatric, and sleep-related pathway scope. The case-control study is the anchor that supplies the significant associations with depressive and anxiety symptoms and altered quality of life in a controlled comparison, together with the violence and injury rates that make the behavioural burden concrete (PMID 23450499). The video-polysomnography cohort is the anchor that supplies the psychiatric comorbidity percentages and, importantly, the finding that ADULT-ONSET AND CHILDHOOD-ONSET SLEEPWALKERS DIFFER, with neurological comorbidity of 44 percent versus 14 percent and EEG abnormality of 50 percent versus 29 percent, which is the located reason the childhood-onset psychological literature cannot simply be transferred to an adult claim (PMID 29073634). The systematic review is the anchor that frames the whole edge, supplying both directions of the relationship and the explicit statement that medications did not significantly bias the results (PMID 39721218). Because the relationship is bidirectional, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, quotes the bidirectionality in the causation status, and requires a temporal determination before any individual attribution. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence is BIDIRECTIONAL, which is stated by the systematic review itself rather than inferred. That review reports findings in both directions, that psychopathology is more common in people with NREM parasomnias AND that parasomnias are more common in people with psychopathology, and concludes only that psychopathological aspects should become a core focus of research and treatment strategies, which is a call for work rather than a directional finding (PMID 39721218). The primary anchor is a cross-sectional case-control study and therefore establishes that depression and anxiety symptoms are MORE COMMON in sleepwalkers than in matched controls, which is a co-occurrence and not a temporal claim, and its population is drawn from a specialist sleep disorders centre and is enriched for severe and complicated presentations including a 57.9 percent rate of violent sleep behaviours (PMID 23450499). The second anchor is a 63-participant specialist video-polysomnography cohort reporting psychiatric comorbidity in a quarter to a third of participants, without a control group, so its percentages are uninterpretable as rates (PMID 29073634). Individual claims therefore require a dated sleepwalking diagnosis with, where claimed, a dated depressive-disorder diagnosis, and a clinical determination of which condition is antecedent, because the located evidence supports the association in both directions and because the majority of the located sleepwalking literature concerns childhood-onset presentations whose psychological trajectory differs from the adult-onset presentations these cohorts describe. Evidence gaps carried openly: The primary anchor is cross-sectional and drawn from a single specialist sleep centre, so it establishes co-occurrence with a matched control group but no temporal order, and its population is enriched for complicated presentations, with 57.9 percent reporting violent sleep behaviours and 17 percent requiring medical care for at least one injury episode (PMID 23450499). The second anchor is a 63-participant specialist cohort with NO CONTROL GROUP, so its psychiatric comorbidity figures of 33 percent and 25 percent are uninterpretable as rates, and its composition of 73 percent childhood-onset and 27 percent adult-onset may not reflect a given claimant (PMID 29073634). The third anchor is a systematic review that, while comprehensive, reports a relationship in BOTH DIRECTIONS and draws no directional conclusion, so it cannot supply causation (PMID 39721218). NO located anchor establishes that treating the sleepwalking reduces depressive symptoms, and no located anchor reports depressive-disorder incidence in an unselected sleepwalking population. A CHILDHOOD-ONLY COUNTERWEIGHT was reviewed and is recorded in the evidence gaps: a longitudinal cohort of 345 healthy children found that more frequent disorders of arousal at age 4 predicted more internalising and externalising problems AT AGE 4 but that at age 5 the association with concurrent problems had DISAPPEARED, with only externalising problems at 5 remaining associated, which is exactly the kind of attenuation that prevents a childhood cohort from being read as a causal claim in an adult. Anchors: PMID 23450499, PMID 29073634, PMID 39721218.
