publicationGuard.structuredGuardText: Publishes as association only (NOT_ESTABLISHED, hypothesizedOnly), mechanism METABOLIC_OR_NUTRITIONAL, with the mechanistic vector named as hypothesized: The hypothesised vector is that a small intestinal tumour ulcerates the mucosa of a segment that standard upper endoscopy reaches poorly and standard lower endoscopy does not reach at all, so that chronic low-volume blood loss goes unobserved, iron is lost without replacement, and the resulting iron deficiency anaemia becomes the presenting feature that eventually triggers capsule or double-balloon enteroscopy, at which point the tumour is found. The vector is named as an occult-loss pathway rather than as a general consequence of malignancy, because the located evidence describes this route specifically, and because a small intestinal tumour can equally present by obstruction, perforation or metastases without any anaemia at all, which is the alternative named first among those to rule out. Conservative basis: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at literature-review-with-case-reports, single-centre-diagnostic-yield-audit, and case-report class, following the file's existing haematological, gastrointestinal, and oncological pathway scope. The literature review is the anchor that supplies the clinical route from ulceration and bleeding through a poorly visualised segment to an iron deficiency workup as the route to diagnosis (PMID 34531134). The diagnostic-yield audit is the anchor that QUANTIFIES THE PATHWAY, reporting how often the small bowel is the site identified after a negative bidirectional endoscopy, and it is the anchor that makes the edge a statement about diagnostic sequence rather than about a complication rate (PMID 42367528). The case report is registered as the MECHANISTIC ILLUSTRATION and is disclosed as the weakest source class in the edge, being a single patient, included because it makes the duodenal presentation concrete and because the three-reference cap would otherwise exclude the only anchor describing the mechanism directly in this segment (PMID 42281724). Because no anchor supplies a rate, the conservative standard holds the edge at association only, names the route rather than a consequence, and requires an explicit alternative-source search before attribution. Causation and direction limits: Neither causation nor aggravation is established for any individual, and the located evidence for this edge is the WEAKEST in the batch, which is stated here rather than implied by its rank. None of the three anchors reports the PROPORTION of patients with small intestinal cancer who were anaemic, or the proportion of patients presenting with iron deficiency anaemia who were found to have a small intestinal tumour; the audit reports diagnostic YIELD after a negative bidirectional endoscopy rather than an association between anaemia and small bowel cancer, and the two remaining anchors are a literature review with case reports and a single case report. The edge is therefore a claim about a PRESENTATION ROUTE and a diagnostic pathway, not about a complication rate, and the causation status says so explicitly: a patient who is anaemic has not thereby been shown to have a small intestinal tumour, and a patient with a small intestinal tumour has not thereby been shown to be anaemic because of it. Individual claims require a dated small intestinal cancer diagnosis with the histological type and segment documented, a dated anaemia diagnosis with a documented iron status and an explicit search for an alternative source, and a clinical determination that the anaemia was attributable to the lesion, which requires excluding the far more common alternative of an unrelated iron deficiency with an incidental small bowel lesion found on the same imaging. Evidence gaps carried openly: NO ANCHOR IN THIS EDGE REPORTS A RATE. None states the prevalence of anaemia among patients with small intestinal cancer or the proportion of iron deficiency anaemia workups that terminate in a small bowel tumour, so the edge cannot carry a magnitude and does not state one. The literature review is a REVIEW WITH CASE REPORTS, which is narrative class and is subject to publication bias toward the unusual (PMID 34531134). The audit is a SINGLE-CENTRE DIAGNOSTIC YIELD STUDY whose denominator is patients with a negative bidirectional endoscopy, so it describes the yield of the investigation that follows the anaemia rather than the association between anaemia and the tumour, and its single-centre design limits transferability (PMID 42367528). The third anchor is a SINGLE CASE REPORT and is the weakest source class available (PMID 42281724). The located evidence is also SEGMENT-INCONSISTENT: small intestinal cancer is not one disease but includes adenocarcinoma, neuroendocrine tumour and gastrointestinal stromal tumour, and the located SEER analysis reports adenocarcinoma predominant in the duodenum at 51.4 percent and neuroendocrine tumour most common in the ileum at 84.21 percent, so an anaemia route derived from duodenal ulceration cannot be transferred to an ileal neuroendocrine tumour, which is the more common histology overall. THAT SEGMENT AND HISTOLOGY MISMATCH IS THE REASON THIS EDGE IS RANKED SECOND, below the thromboembolism edge, whose located evidence is drawn from a 205-million-hospitalisation analysis covering gastrointestinal cancers as a class. Alternatives requiring exclusion before any individual attribution: A benign source of iron deficiency, including menstrual or gastrointestinal blood loss unrelated to the tumour, which is the far more common explanation in the general population and must be actively excluded rather than assumed absent; Coeliac disease and other malabsorptive causes of iron deficiency, which can coexist with and independently explain an anaemia in the same patient; Chronic kidney disease and systemic inflammatory conditions, both of which are registered catalog identities with their own established routes to anaemia and both of which would supply an alternative explanation; Neuroendocrine tumour of the small bowel, which is the most common histology overall and whose presentation is more often hormonal, obstructive or incidental than anaemic, so the anaemia route is not applicable to it; A gastrointestinal stromal tumour, which is a distinct entity the catalog already carries separately and whose bleeding pattern differs from that of an epithelial malignancy.
